title: Thinner Every Time
logline: A potter throws a nested set of bowls in one sitting, each wall thinner than the last, judging by feel alone the exact point where thinner would mean broken.
human_question: Is getting subtler the same as getting better, and how do you know when you have gone as far as this material will let you?

premise.story: A potter makes a graduated set of bowls or pots, from the thickest to the thinnest they can safely throw, in one working session.
premise.experience: The visible, tactile logic of refinement: each vessel possible only because the last one was mastered first.

concept_links.why: The source describes each higher absorption as reached only by seeing that the previous one, though good, is comparatively coarse, and letting it go; its own simile is four cloths of equal size woven from coarser to finer thread [C088-P4:L280–L284]. The film substitutes a potter's graduated vessels for the same idea of successive refinement.
Each subtler state is described as resting on the one before it, like men hanging from a roof, one holding the one below [C014-P:L68]; the nested bowls hold the same relationship physically.

The source notes that some learn a sequence in fewer, larger steps and others need more, smaller ones; if there are two potters, or a master and apprentice, at different paces, the film can show that difference honestly [C015-P:L45–L47].

what_camera_could_observe: The thickest bowl thrown first, then progressively thinner ones from the same batch of clay
The potter's hands judging thickness by feel, not by measurement
A wall that collapses because it was pushed too thin
The finished graduated set, nested, at the end of the session
what_must_be_real: The potter's actual practice and judgement, including real failures. No claim is made that the craft is itself meditation.

possible_arc.opening: Clay centred on the wheel, the first, thickest bowl.
possible_arc.turn: A collapsed attempt at the thinnest wall.
possible_arc.ending_open: The finished set, or the honest account of how far the potter could safely go that day.

requirements: A working potter skilled in graduated or fine-walled ware
A willingness to attempt several vessels in sequence for the camera
Good light for close hand-work photography

suggestions.name: A traditional pottery village
suggestions.region: Low country wet zone or North Western Province
suggestions.why: Pottery is a long-standing craft in several villages in this region.
suggestions.verify: A specific willing potter and village must be identified.

risks: Forcing the refinement metaphor onto ordinary craft variation
Romanticising a livelihood under economic pressure
drop_if: No potter is willing to attempt a real graduated set on camera, or the craft does not naturally work this way

connections.note: Both are close studies of craft attention narrowing and refining, one on a single stone, one across a graduated set of vessels.
Refinement of depth here; refinement of texture, not destination, in the ferry crossing.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
